text:
mina: Flagging a docs mismatch for /v1/uploads. The API reference shows only JSON/base64 payloads (file field) but hosted endpoints require multipart/form-data. I tried the JSON example and got 415 Unsupported Media Type.

igor: Thanks, Mina. We should make multipart the canonical example and keep JSON/base64 as an alternate for Dedicated/private installs that enable legacy_uploads.

tess: Agreed. Proposed edits: update OpenAPI requestBody to allow both media types (oneOf), render multipart/form-data first in examples, add an "Alternate: JSON (base64)" callout with a clear Hosted vs Dedicated note, and add SDK convenience snippets.

mina: Multipart cURL we'll use in the ref:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/uploads \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -F "file=@./pic.png" \
  -F "filename=pic.png"
# curl sets Content-Type: multipart/form-data automatically
```

mina: Short python SDK example too:
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
cl = RedwoodClient(REDWOOD_KEY)
cl.upload_file(path='pic.png', filename='pic.png')
```

ops-bot: Preview deployed for PR 949 123: https://docs-preview.redwood.ai/pr/949/uploads-multipart. Please check wording on legacy flag.

igor: I'll open the PR and ping SANJAY for technical review on the legacy_uploads wording. Also add note: Hosted max file size 25 MB; Dedicated tunable.

tess: Small docs nit: explicitly mention Content-Type line in cURL (even though curl adds it) and add guidance to stream files for large uploads in code samples.

mina: Sounds good. Assigning reviews: igor (author), sanjay (tech), tess (docs).
